A later current-build INIT descriptor scan then found the matching value-name binding row pointing at the same live global RVA, which closes the static registry-seeding layer for the candidate. setting.name: Win32k Callout Watchdog Timeout Seconds
setting.casual_explanation: This appears to be a low-level power-manager watchdog timeout for Win32k callouts. On the observed clean baseline the registry value is not configured, but the running kernel still keeps an in-memory default.
setting.why_people_change_it: Kernel and power researchers may inspect this value when tracing Win32k callout watchdog behavior and watchdog packet timing in the power manager.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: The candidate now has repo routing, clean-baseline absence, exact current-build string presence, a live current-build consumer path, and a current-build INIT descriptor binding for the same global. It is still too weak for a published tweak because exact runtime registry-read proof and non-default override semantics remain unresolved.
setting.professional_notes: The repo docs-first power routing pass already listed `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Power\\Win32kCalloutWatchdogTimeoutSeconds` as a new candidate. A later existence-first pass on the observed clean baseline confirmed that the `Control\\Power` path exists while the value itself is absent. A later targeted current-build string batch found an exact Unicode hit for `Win32kCalloutWatchdogTimeoutSeconds` in `C:\\Windows\\System32\\ntoskrnl.exe`. A later KVM local-KD follow-up then resolved the live current-build watchdog-family cluster around `PopInvokeWin32CalloutWithWatchdog` and directly read `PopWin32kCalloutWatchdogTimeoutSeconds = 0x1e` (`30`). The same pass disassembled `PopInvokeWin32CalloutWithWatchdog` and showed a direct `imul` against the global by `1000`, followed by the watchdog packet path through `ZwPowerInformation` and the surrounding Win32 callout path. That is materially stronger than a string-only or sibling-only clue: the running kernel is actively consuming the global even though the registry value is missing on the observed baseline. The main open question is whether the registry value is an optional override on top of a built-in 30-second default, or whether a boot-only helper still seeds the same global from `Control\\Power` when present. A later host-side current-build INIT descriptor scan found the `Win32kCalloutWatchdogTimeoutSeconds` UTF-16 string in `ntoskrnl.exe` and one nearby row at file offset `0xbee0e8` pointing at static RVA `0xE0B518`, matching the live KD RVA for `nt!PopWin32kCalloutWatchdogTimeoutSeconds`. The nearest retained key-context string in that row family is the generic `Power` label rather than a longer decoded `Control\Power` path, but the row/global alignment is still current-build specific and closes the static registry-seeding layer.
